A call through a proxy keeps its Call-ID, so sipnab sees one call. A call
through a back-to-back user agent (B2BUA) does not. A PBX such as Asterisk or
FreeSWITCH, an SBC, and OpenSIPS with topology hiding end the call on one side
and start a new one on the other, each with its own Call-ID. sipnab then holds
two calls, or more across several hops, and ties them together.

This page shows how to list a call's other legs, how to read how sipnab tied
each one, and what to change on your SIP servers so the tie is an exact match
rather than a guess.

## What you need

- A sipnab build with the default features, for everything except decoding
  OpenSIPS topology-hiding Call-IDs, which needs the `tls` feature. Every
  release package has it.
- Reading a capture file needs no privileges. A live capture needs root or
  `CAP_NET_RAW`.
- A capture that holds every leg. Capture where the legs meet, on the B2BUA
  itself or on a link that carries both sides. sipnab cannot join a leg the
  capture does not hold.
- A change on your SIP servers only if you want an exact match where there is
  none today. [Make the match exact](#make-the-match-exact) says what to change
  for each server.

## List the other legs of a call

Name one leg with `--correlate`. This capture holds one call through an
Asterisk PBX: the caller's leg, and the leg Asterisk placed to the callee.

```sh
sipnab -I tests/pcap-samples/b2bua-asterisk.pcapng --correlate b2bua-caller-synth@203.0.113.1 --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Legs correlated with b2bua-caller-synth@203.0.113.1: 1 leg
Leg                                 Strategy          Method  Score  Match  Gap ms
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
b2bua-leg-synth@203.0.113.101:5060  timing_heuristic  timing  50     guess  3
Every leg here is a timing guess: no identifier ties it to this call.
```

- `Strategy` names the rule that tied the leg. `Method` says what sipnab
  compared the two legs on.
- `Match` is `identifier` when both legs carry the same identifier, and
  `guess` when only their timing and addresses tie them.
- `Gap ms` is how far apart the two legs started, for a guess.

Here Asterisk wrote nothing into the callee's leg that names the caller's, so
the tie is a guess. A guess can join unrelated calls on a busy server. [Make the match exact](#make-the-match-exact) changes it to
an identifier match.

`--report` lists the Call-IDs a capture holds. The Call-ID must match exactly.

### Walk a call across several hops

A call through an SBC and then a PBX has three legs or more. `--call-tree`
follows the ties leg by leg and prints the whole call. This capture's calls
cross one hop, so each tree has two legs:

```sh
sipnab -I tests/fixtures/session-id/opensips-4.0-th-session-id.pcap --call-tree 1-sid-call@example.com --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Call tree from 1-sid-call@example.com: 2 legs, depth 1, 13 messages, 0 timing guesses
Leg                                       Strategy    Method  Score  Match       Followed
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1-sid-call@example.com                    root        -       -      -           yes
  DLGCH_fl0WBzdkMzIjHCULKyg9IyMVSw08JA--  session_id  header  100    identifier  yes
```

- Each hop indents the leg two more spaces.
- `Followed` is `no` on a guess: sipnab lists the leg but does not look for
  that leg's own matches, so one wrong guess cannot pull in unrelated calls.

## Read how sipnab tied each leg

sipnab tries each strategy, and reports a leg under the highest-scoring one
that matched.

| Strategy | Method | Score | What both legs carry | What it needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | `header` | 100 | The same [RFC 7989](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7989.html) `Session-ID` | Endpoints or a server that send it. Nothing in sipnab |
| `th_callid_decoded` | `decoded` | 100 | A Call-ID that OpenSIPS `topology_hiding("C")` encoded, which decodes to the other leg's | The OpenSIPS secret in `[sip] th_callid_secret_file` |
| `th_callid_mapping` | `mapping` | 100 | Nothing: OpenSIPS sends sipnab the pair | An OpenSIPS event to sipnab's HEP listener |
| `x_call_id` | `header` | 100 | A header, named in `[sip] xcid_headers`, holding the other leg's Call-ID | A header your server adds, and its name in sipnab's configuration |
| `charging_vector_related_icid` | `header` | 95 | An [RFC 7315](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7315.html) `P-Charging-Vector` whose `related-icid` names the other leg's `icid-value` | An IMS or carrier B2BUA that sends it |
| `sdp_origin` | `sdp` | 90 | The same SDP origin line, while both legs were open, and an origin no two calls in the capture used on one hop at once | A server that passes SDP through unchanged, and endpoints that write a new origin for each call |
| `charging_vector_icid` | `header` | 85 | The same `P-Charging-Vector` `icid-value` | An intermediary that copied it onto the second leg |
| `via_branch` | `header` | 80 | A shared Via branch | A proxy hop, not a B2BUA |
| `timing_heuristic` | `timing` | 50 | Nothing: the legs started close together and share an address | Nothing. A guess |

[Run MCP across an estate](@/docs/mcp-estate.md#choose-a-correlation-identifier)
explains what each identifier proves and where it stops working.

### Read `strategy`, `identifier_match` and the score

Read the three fields of a leg in this order:

1. `strategy` names the rule that tied the leg. It is the decisive field: two
   strategies with one score are not the same claim.
2. `identifier_match` is `true` when the two legs carry one identifier, and
   `false` for `timing_heuristic`, which is a guess.
3. The score orders the strategies. It is a rank, not a probability.

### When an SDP origin counts

[RFC 8866 section 5.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8866.html#section-5.2)
says the origin line's username, session ID, network type, address type and
address are globally unique for a session. Not every endpoint follows that.
SIPp's built-in `uac` scenario writes
`o=user1 53655765 2353687637 IN IP4 <ip>` into every call, and some phones
and gateways write the same session ID into every call. So sipnab reports
`sdp_origin` only when both of these hold:

- The two legs were open at one time. A B2BUA sends the second leg before the
  first one's call setup ends, and both stay up for the call. Calls placed one
  after the other are not open at one time. The time runs from a leg's first
  message to its last, and a leg that starts at the instant the other ended
  still counts.
- No two calls in the capture used the origin on one hop at once. A hop is the
  sending address and the receiving address and port of a leg's first
  message. Each leg of a B2BUA call is a different hop. A load test that places
  overlapping calls with one origin sends them all on one hop, and then the
  origin ties no leg to any other.

An origin line that does not have the six fields of RFC 8866, or whose session
ID or version is not a number, ties nothing.

When the rule refuses a pair, a weaker strategy such as `timing_heuristic` can
still tie it, and sipnab reports it at that strategy's strength.

The rule says less than the truth in three cases:

- A B2BUA that forks one call to two contacts through one next hop.
- A spiral that sends one offer over one hop twice.
- Two capture points whose clocks differ by more than the call lasted.

In each case, give the legs an identifier from
[Make the match exact](#make-the-match-exact).

### What changes for SIPp load tests

A SIPp scenario that writes a constant origin, as the built-in `uac` scenario
does, no longer ties its calls together by the origin:

- Calls placed one after the other each keep their own B2BUA legs.
- Calls that overlap on one hop tie nothing by the origin, not even a call's
  own B2BUA leg. The timing heuristic may still list legs as guesses.

To keep an identifier match in a load test, make the origin unique per call:
write `o=caller [call_number] 1 IN IP[local_ip_type] [local_ip]` in the
scenario, as [`harness/th-callid/uac.xml`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/harness/th-callid/uac.xml) does,
or send `Session-ID` or a correlation header.

To check a capture, list the legs of one call:

```sh
sipnab -I tests/fixtures/th-callid/opensips-4.0-default.pcap --correlate 1-th-call@example.com --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Legs correlated with 1-th-call@example.com: 5 legs
Leg                                 Strategy          Method  Score  Match       Gap ms  TH
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DLGCH_fl0RBn4qMT8jMAAWMiQgPypeBgE+  sdp_origin        sdp     90     identifier  -       no_secret
2-th-call@example.com               timing_heuristic  timing  50     guess       999     -
DLGCH_fV0RBn4qMT8jMAAWMiQgPypeBgE+  timing_heuristic  timing  50     guess       1000    no_secret
3-th-call@example.com               timing_heuristic  timing  50     guess       1999    -
DLGCH_fF0RBn4qMT8jMAAWMiQgPypeBgE+  timing_heuristic  timing  50     guess       2000    no_secret
```

The call's own callee leg is the `sdp_origin` identifier match. The two later
calls, one and two seconds after, are timing guesses.

## Make the match exact

Pick one of these, in this order of preference.

### Pass RFC 7989 Session-ID through

`Session-ID` is a pair of identifiers that the two endpoints of a session
exchange, made to survive a B2BUA. sipnab reads it with no configuration, and
matches the two halves in either order.

This capture holds three calls through OpenSIPS with
`topology_hiding("C")`, which gives the callee's leg a new Call-ID. The
endpoints send `Session-ID`, and OpenSIPS passes it through unchanged:

```sh
sipnab -I tests/fixtures/session-id/opensips-4.0-th-session-id.pcap --correlate 1-sid-call@example.com --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Legs correlated with 1-sid-call@example.com: 1 leg
Leg                                     Strategy    Method  Score  Match       Gap ms
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DLGCH_fl0WBzdkMzIjHCULKyg9IyMVSw08JA--  session_id  header  100    identifier  -
```

Which servers send it:

- **Endpoints and SBCs.** Check whether yours send it:
  `sipnab -N -I capture.pcap --filter "header.Session-ID =~ '.'" --report`
  lists the calls that carry it.
- **FreeSWITCH** writes it when a Sofia profile sets the `rfc-7989` parameter
  to `true`. FreeSWITCH reads the parameter in
  [`src/mod/endpoints/mod_sofia/sofia.c`](https://github.com/signalwire/freeswitch/blob/v1.11.3/src/mod/endpoints/mod_sofia/sofia.c#L5395)
  of FreeSWITCH 1.11.3 (read on 2026-11-03). Not tested with sipnab.
- **OpenSIPS** passes the header through unchanged, as the capture above
  shows for OpenSIPS 4.0.2 through topology hiding. A proxy forwards the
  header fields it does not act on ([RFC 3261 section 16.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3261.html#section-16.6)), so Kamailio as
  a proxy passes it too. Not tested here with Kamailio.
- A search of the OpenSIPS, Kamailio and Asterisk source code on GitHub on
  2026-11-03 found no code that writes the header.

### Copy the caller's Call-ID into a header

Have the B2BUA add a header to the callee's INVITE that holds the caller's
Call-ID, then tell sipnab its name. This header names nothing standard, so
sipnab looks for none until you name one.

**This header discloses the caller's Call-ID to the callee's side.** Add it
only on legs inside your own network, or remove it where the call leaves.

#### On the server

Asterisk 22. A pre-dial handler sets the header on the outbound channel, from
the inbound channel's Call-ID. In `extensions.conf`:

```text
[from-caller]
exten => 100,1,Dial(PJSIP/callee,30,b(add-xcid^s^1(${CHANNEL(pjsip,call-id)})))
 same => n,Hangup()

[add-xcid]
exten => s,1,Set(PJSIP_HEADER(add,X-CID)=${ARG1})
 same => n,Return()
```

Tested on 2026-11-03 with Asterisk 22.11.0: the callee's INVITE carried
`X-CID: 1-xcid-call@example.com`. The capture below is that test.

OpenSIPS with topology hiding. Add `append_hf("X-CID: $ci\r\n");` after
`topology_hiding("C")`. [Run sipnab beside OpenSIPS](@/docs/opensips-sipnab.md#or-copy-the-call-id-into-a-header)
shows the script and the tests that run it. OpenSIPS can also tell sipnab the
pair with no header at all. That section describes both.

Kamailio with the topology-hiding module and `mask_callid = 1`, which encodes
the Call-ID ([module documentation](https://www.kamailio.org/docs/modules/6.1.x/modules/topoh.html#topoh.p.mask_callid),
read on 2026-11-03). Add the header in the request route before the request
leaves, with
[`append_hf`](https://www.kamailio.org/docs/modules/6.1.x/modules/textops.html#textops.f.append_hf):

```text
append_hf("X-CID: $ci\r\n");
```

Not tested: the Kamailio build on this project's test host lacks that
module. Check on the wire that the callee's INVITE carries the caller's
Call-ID before you rely on it.

FreeSWITCH. Set a `sip_h_` channel variable before the `bridge`. FreeSWITCH
adds a header named after the prefix to the outbound INVITE, and
`sip_call_id` holds the inbound leg's Call-ID
([channel variables](https://developer.signalwire.com/freeswitch/reference/channel-variables#sip-custom-headers),
read on 2026-11-03):

```xml
<action application="set" data="sip_h_X-CID=${sip_call_id}"/>
<action application="bridge" data="user/1000"/>
```

Not tested with sipnab.

#### In sipnab

Name the header in the `[sip]` section of the configuration file:

```toml
[sip]
xcid_headers = ["X-CID"]
```

Without it, the Asterisk capture's legs tie only by timing:

```sh
sipnab -I tests/fixtures/xcid/asterisk-22-xcid.pcap --correlate 1-xcid-call@example.com --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Legs correlated with 1-xcid-call@example.com: 1 leg
Leg                                   Strategy          Method  Score  Match  Gap ms
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
207e9af6-c60c-4f7f-99ae-328d569004c6  timing_heuristic  timing  50     guess  5
Every leg here is a timing guess: no identifier ties it to this call.
```

With it, they tie on the header:

```sh
sipnab -I tests/fixtures/xcid/asterisk-22-xcid.pcap --config sipnab.toml --correlate 1-xcid-call@example.com --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Legs correlated with 1-xcid-call@example.com: 1 leg
Leg                                   Strategy   Method  Score  Match       Gap ms
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
207e9af6-c60c-4f7f-99ae-328d569004c6  x_call_id  header  100    identifier  -
```

`xcid_headers` takes a list, so one sipnab can read the headers of several
servers.

### Use OpenSIPS's own help with topology hiding

OpenSIPS with `topology_hiding("C")` can tie its legs for sipnab in two more
ways: sipnab decodes the hidden Call-ID with OpenSIPS's secret, or OpenSIPS
sends sipnab each pair as an event.
[Calls through topology hiding](@/docs/opensips-sipnab.md#calls-through-topology-hiding)
gives the steps for both.

### Widen the guess for a slow PBX

When no identifier crosses a hop, the timing guess is what remains. It ties
two legs that started within two seconds of each other and share an address.
A PBX that looks a number up before it places the second leg (an LNP or ENUM
query, a routing list) can start it later than that, and the guess then
misses. Widen the window, in milliseconds:

```sh
sipnab -I tests/pcap-samples/b2bua-asterisk.pcapng --leg-correlation-window 8000 --correlate b2bua-caller-synth@203.0.113.1 --no-cli-print --quiet
```

The configuration key is `[sip] leg_correlation_window_ms`. A wider window
also ties more unrelated calls on a busy server, which `Gap ms` shows.

## Ask the same question elsewhere

| Where | How |
|---|---|
| Command line | `--correlate <CALL-ID>`, `--call-tree <CALL-ID>`, each with `--json` |
| REST | `GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}/correlated`, `GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}/tree` |
| MCP | `find_correlated`, `get_call_tree` |
| Terminal interface | In the call flow, `x` or `F4` draws the related legs in one ladder |
| vCon | The `sipnab-related-legs` attachment of an exported call |

Every surface reports the same `strategy` and `method` for each leg. Under
`--json`, `--correlate` prints the answer the REST route returns:

```sh
sipnab -I tests/fixtures/session-id/opensips-4.0-th-session-id.pcap --correlate 1-sid-call@example.com --json --no-cli-print --quiet | jq -c '.legs[] | {call_id, strategy, method, identifier_match}'
```

```json
{"call_id":"DLGCH_fl0WBzdkMzIjHCULKyg9IyMVSw08JA--","strategy":"session_id","method":"header","identifier_match":true}
```

## When it does not work

| What you see | Why | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `--correlate` prints no legs | The capture does not hold the other leg, or nothing ties it | Capture where both legs pass. Check with `--report` that both are there |
| The legs tie with `timing_heuristic` although the server adds a header | `[sip] xcid_headers` does not name the header, or sipnab did not read the configuration file | Name the header. Pass `--config` with the file, and check that sipnab does not print that it ignores a configuration file |
| The legs tie with `timing_heuristic` and a large `Gap ms`, or not at all | The B2BUA placed the second leg later than the window | Widen `--leg-correlation-window`, or add an identifier |
| Unrelated calls appear as legs | Timing guesses on a busy server | Read `Match`. Add an identifier, so the guess is not needed |
| Two legs that share an SDP origin are not tied by `sdp_origin` | The legs were not open at one time, or other calls in the capture used the origin on one hop at once | See [When an SDP origin counts](#when-an-sdp-origin-counts). Make the origin unique per call, or add an identifier |
| Exit 1 and `no dialog with Call-ID` | The Call-ID is not in the capture, or is not exact | Copy it from `--report` |
| A topology-hiding leg reports `th_callid` `undecodable` or `unmatched` | The secret or prefix is wrong, or the caller's leg is missing | See [Calls through topology hiding](@/docs/opensips-sipnab.md#calls-through-topology-hiding) |
